Oh, what is this?
Hmm...
Hmm?

It's not like I can turn him down...
I'll have to find a way to convince Grams.
Mugwort dumplings! Mugwort dumplings!
Wait right there!
Hey! What are you doing?!

It looks similar, but it's not.
If you make dumplings  out of this, you'll die.
What?! Then what about my dumplings?!
Give it up.

You found some yesterday, didn't you?
I need it for moxibustion.
Stingy!
Ow! You're horrible!
Who's horrible here?
Besides, I told you not to  loiter around by yourself.
Sazen was with us!
Huh?
Don't leave me behind!
I'm not that young, you know.
If the brat won't learn, I guess  I have to teach the chaperone.
Just wait.
Do you know what these are?
Yeah, mugwort and wolfsbane, right?
I was going to swap them later,  but he ran off.
Here you are.
Mugwort!
Let's go!
This is for you.
Wolfsbane root.
I pulled it up because it's dangerous,
but it's useful in medicine  if you dry it, right?
Aconiti tuber, was it?
It would be a waste to just let it rot.
What did he just say?
How does he know the name of  the medicinal form of wolfsbane root?
Someone probably brought it down the  mountain because the flower was pretty—
What's this?
Medlar leaf.
The effects?
It stops coughs and diarrhea,  and other things, I think.
And this?
Goldthread, good for the stomach.
And mental stability, I think.
And this?
Plantain, of course...
What's this about?
Just continue!
Huh...?
I guess you know about half of these.
Seriously, what's this about?
Can you read?
Huh? Yeah, the old man  at the stronghold taught me.
Did he teach you about herbs, too?
Yeah.
I see.
This I did not see coming.
It'll be a rush job,  but it just might work.
Alright, memorize this!
And come work with me  during the day from now on.
Huh?! I have my own job, too—
I'll talk to Grams and Ukyou.
Besides, you're not that good at  the work the menservants do, are you?
Um... Well, uh...
Maybe you'll be better off  as an apothecary?
Since I'm connected with Master Nhâm Thị,  I'll need to be away from this place often.
If Sazen can be an apothecary...
I'm just a farmer.
The only reason I went to that  stronghold was because I was broke.
So, I mean, I was only following  the old man's instructions for the herbs...
So what?
Some people make a living off casting  weird curses on people with colds.
You, on the other hand, can make  a simple cure for a fever, right?
I mean, yeah, but...  What about seriously sick people?
If you can't handle it, just say so.
Huh?
Some people die, whether  they take medicine or not.
Pass them off to someone else.  Better than pretending you have a cure.
You'd be surprised how many doctors  are worse at making medicine than you.
Like a certain quack doctor.
Okay, it's settled.
Whoa.
Memorize all of these.  I'll go talk to Grams.
Isn't this all a bit too sudden?
I have to hurry. I don't have time.
As I expected, Sazen was a quick study.
He learned simple recipes quickly,  and could read books, though clumsily.
I'm trying to teach Chou-u  as well, just in case,
but the brat shows zero interest.
I'm going to deliver  the medicine next door.
Yes.
This will work.
What are you doing here?
Maomao, wait for me!
Little lady, long time no see.
Phew! Finally caught my breath.
Anyway, what brings you here?
What about your job at the rear palace—
Oh.
He must've finally gotten fired.
He's really nice, but totally  worthless as a doctor.
Never mind.
Little lady, aren't you  misunderstanding something?
I was allowed to take a vacation.
I'm going to visit my family back home.
Ah, you're being sent home.
You're doing that on purpose, aren't you?
They added an odd condition  to my trip, though.
Has anyone talked to you  about it, by any chance?
What condition?
I've been told that someone  wants to come along.
The head of the eunuchs asked me.  Sounded like someone important.
They wanted me to meet them here.
I see.
I was hoping I'd get more time.
I'm going on a trip. Come with me.
Master Nhâm Thị's message was unilateral,
and said nothing about the duration,  destination, or even a departure date.
So I taught Sazen medicine  as fast as I could.
I also made a lot of medicine in advance.
But why the quack doctor?
And also...
Oh, a cat!
Oh!
Ouch! Oh, wait!
Thank you for the food!
Hmm?
Who's this, now?
Hey!
What's with this cat?!
The dining room!
Who are you?
I'm really sorry.
Come on, be nice, Maomao.
Maomao? What kind of name is that?
Shut up.
Look after her.
Don't let her get away.
Got it!
I've decided to ask my family  to look after Maomao.
I'm the only one that can take  care of her at the rear palace.
Princess Lingli left the rear palace  with Empress Ngọc Diệp, right?
They weren't allowed  to take the cat along.
I guess they got shut down  by those around them.
I'm sure there's more rules  than the rear palace.
My little sister will be glad  to have a rat hunter.
Is that the person who sent you  letters regarding papermaking?
That's right.
But this time, she sent me  something concerning.
What was it?
I shouldn't talk about it here...
I'll explain when we get to the village.
Are you ready to leave?
Master Basen. Why are you dressed like—
Am I ready? Isn't this a bit sudden?
We have our reasons.
A reason important enough  to put on disguises, huh?
Well done. It's like he's  Master Basen's servant.
The quack doctor doesn't even realize.
Master Basen does seem rather  uncomfortable, though.
Get in. We've prepared  your luggage already.
Yes.
This seems like it's going  to be a long, secret trip.
It must be tough for him.  He's busy enough as it is.
The emperor sure does like to  put his little brother to work.
It's almost as if he's  training a successor...
Not gonna go there.
There's already a prince.
Lady Lê Hoa gave birth to a boy, too.
And the emperor himself is still young.
No sense in thinking disturbing thoughts.
Two days in a horse carriage.
The quack doctor's hometown is  to the southwest of the capital.
That's barley.
The irrigation seems  very well developed here.
It's for rice farming in the summer.
Rice and barley. We grow  two crops over one year.
Paddy rice can be grown on  the same soil without impoverishing it.
It must be a fertile region.
The river's nearby, too.  Must be good for transportation.
He isn't used to cats?
This man has a lot of weaknesses.
Hmm?
What was that?
Oh, my dear brother! Welcome home.
Yes, I'm home.
Is this the cat?
Oh, how cute!
More importantly, are these your guests?
Y-Yes.
Is that so? Your boss  at work and his assistant?
Assistant, huh?
Thank you for your hospitality.
Please don't mention it. Enjoy your stay.
Oh!
Yum!
Well, goodness.
For a moment, I thought my eunuch  brother brought back a young wife!
Haha, that's impossible.
Indeed.
Oh, dear. Are you alright?
If you're pretending to be a servant,
just stay in the carriage and  eat preserved foods or something.
Of course, Master Basen  wouldn't allow that.
It'd be a shame to ruin  his perfect disguise,
so I hope he doesn't do anything weird.
I'm back.
Oh, I'm so hungry!
Brother! Long time no see.
Indeed, long time no see!
It's great to see you again, Uncle.
Yes, you've grown a lot bigger.
Oh...
Hey, where are your manners?!
Bro...
That's the quack's nephew, right?
The older son's quite rude.
He's a eunuch who's been gone for years.
Why would you bring him back now?
And with a bunch of guests in tow.
Why would you say that?!
I'll take this, I don't want it  to get cold.
Wha...
Where's my soup?
Don't you have something  else to say first?!
Dammit.
I'm sorry. He doesn't understand how  much you've done for the village, Brother.
It's fine. I'm used to this type of thing.
If I remember right, quack doctor went  to work at the rear palace in her stead.
That must pain her quite a bit.
But...
No, I must apologize for  barging in so suddenly.
Anyway, you reached out to me because  you needed me for something, right?
Don't you have something to discuss?
To tell you the truth...
There's a request we want  to make of the emperor!
Huh?!
Brother, you're a great doctor who helped  birth the emperor's children, right?!
That was my dad, but...
I guess he exaggerated it to his family.
I'm not going to out him  or anything, but...
Look at them, staring into the distance.
I'm not worthy! I'm in no  position to speak to him!
Is there no way?
Well...
I can't speak with the emperor,  but there may be others I can talk to.
What is this about, anyway?
Could you share with us?
I don't know how much  help we can be, but...
Don't worry. These are proper officials.
If you say so...
It's about the rights  to the land this village is on.
This was originally a borrowed plot.
According to the husband, the previous  landlord was a generous person.
He let the villagers borrow the land  at a bargain, as he wasn't using it.
As the years went by, they started  discussing purchasing the land.
They signed a deal to purchase  the land and forest over 20 years.
Payment proceeded without issue.
But a few years ago,  the landlord passed away.
His son took over,  and things changed from there.
The new landlord doesn't like outsiders,
and also has a general  disrespect for craftsmen.
He was annoyed at how their paper led  them to be purveyors to the emperor.
When the quality of the paper  went down that one time,
he kept showing up to  demand payment on the loan.
He's harassed us often before.
He told us that we dirty the water  and ruin the rice yields,
or that we used up the water  and now they can't grow rice.
But this time, it was more serious.
He told us to pay immediately or leave.
How many years of payment are left?
Five. There's no way we can  pay in one lump sum.
The current landlord wants  to take over the papermaking.
Why? Why not just let us do our thing?
It's because the tax on grains  went up a lot suddenly this year.
Meanwhile, the tax on papermaking  went down a few years ago.
That must annoy him, too.
The tax cut on paper must  have been to increase literacy.
The tax hike on grains, on the other  hand, must be for the locust plague.
Given the double crop  yield from this region,
the tax hike shouldn't be enough  to cause any real problems.
But still, it's not easy being  on the receiving end of that.
And on top of that, there's him.
For a few reasons, my older son  sided with the farmers.
Also, he believes  all bureaucrats are the same.
That's why I wanted to see if we  could ask for a tax cut on grains.
I'm just a eunuch.
I see.
Well, in that case, we're having  a discussion tomorrow.
Can you come along?
I can do that.
May I join as well?
I... I don't know if the other  party would like that.
Having a third party present  might be helpful in some way.
I won't interject. If they refuse,  I can speak with them.
I guess he's concerned,  since he's part of it.
In that case, I suppose...
I'll make sure to be there, too!
Not that you're going to be of any use.
Come on, don't cry. Please.
But... At this rate...
Don't worry.
I'll handle this.
